problems.title: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'requests' after pip install
problems.body:
I ran pip install requests and it says 'Requirement already satisfied', but running my script still fails with:
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "app.py", line 1, in <module>
    import requests
ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'requests'
I am running the script from VS Code.

solutions.body: pip and python point at different interpreters. Install with the same interpreter that runs the script, and select that interpreter (or your venv) in VS Code.
steps: Print the interpreter running the script: python -c "import sys; print(sys.executable)"
Install using that exact interpreter: python -m pip install requests
In VS Code run 'Python: Select Interpreter' and pick the same interpreter or .venv
solutions.code:
python -c "import sys; print(sys.executable)"
python -m pip install requests

problems.title: pip install fails with error: externally-managed-environment
problems.body:
On Ubuntu 24.04, pip install fails:
error: externally-managed-environment
× This environment is externally managed
╰─> To install Python packages system-wide, try apt install python3-xyz
How do I install packages now?

solutions.body: PEP 668 marks the system Python as managed by apt. Create a virtual environment for your project and install packages inside it.
solutions.code:
sudo apt install python3-venv
python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate
pip install requests

solutions.body: Force the install into the system interpreter with --break-system-packages. It works but can break apt-managed tools; prefer a venv or pipx.

problems.title: A module that was compiled using NumPy 1.x cannot be run in NumPy 2.0.0
problems.body:
After upgrading packages, importing pandas crashes:
A module that was compiled using NumPy 1.x cannot be run in
NumPy 2.0.0 as it may crash. To support both 1.x and 2.x versions of NumPy, modules must be compiled with NumPy 2.0.
ImportError: numpy.core.multiarray failed to import

solutions.body: Upgrade the package that was built against NumPy 1.x to a release built for NumPy 2 (pandas 2.2.2 or newer).
Pin NumPy below 2 until all dependencies support it.

problems.title: SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED on macOS with python.org installer
problems.body:
urllib and requests fail with:
ssl.SSLCertVerificationError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate (_ssl.c:1006)
Python was installed from the python.org .pkg installer.

solutions.body: The python.org macOS build does not use the system keychain. Run the bundled 'Install Certificates.command' to install certifi's CA bundle.

problems.title: 'pip' is not recognized as an internal or external command
problems.body:
On Windows 11, running pip in Command Prompt prints:
'pip' is not recognized as an internal or external command,
operable program or batch file.
Python itself is installed.

solutions.body: Use the Python launcher, which is always on PATH, to run pip as a module. To fix the PATH permanently, re-run the installer and tick 'Add python.exe to PATH'.

problems.title: UnicodeDecodeError: 'charmap' codec can't decode byte 0x9d
problems.body:
Reading a text file works on my Mac but on Windows fails with:
UnicodeDecodeError: 'charmap' codec can't decode byte 0x9d in position 1523: character maps to <undefined>

solutions.body: On Windows open() defaults to the ANSI code page (cp1252). Pass the encoding explicitly.
solutions.code:
with open("data.txt", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    text = f.read()

solutions.body: Enable Python UTF-8 mode globally so the default encoding is UTF-8. Fixes your code but not third-party code that hard-codes another encoding.

problems.title: error: Microsoft Visual C++ 14.0 or greater is required
problems.body:
pip install fails while building a wheel:
error: Microsoft Visual C++ 14.0 or greater is required. Get it with "Microsoft C++ Build Tools": https://visualstudio.microsoft.com/visual-cpp-build-tools/
ERROR: Failed building wheel

solutions.body: Install the Build Tools for Visual Studio with the 'Desktop development with C++' workload, then retry the install.
steps: Select the 'Desktop development with C++' workload and install
Open a new terminal and re-run pip install

solutions.body: Use a Python version the package ships prebuilt wheels for, so nothing has to be compiled.

problems.title: django.db.utils.OperationalError: no such table
problems.body:
Opening the admin page raises:
django.db.utils.OperationalError: no such table: blog_post
I just added the Post model.

solutions.body: The table was never created. Generate and apply migrations for the app.
solutions.code:
python manage.py makemigrations blog
python manage.py migrate

problems.title: Error: Cannot find module 'express'
problems.body:
node server.js fails with:
Error: Cannot find module 'express'
Require stack:
- /home/me/app/server.js
    at Module._resolveFilename (node:internal/modules/cjs/loader:1145:15)
  code: 'MODULE_NOT_FOUND'

solutions.body: Dependencies are not installed in this project folder. Run npm install from the folder containing package.json (or add express if it is missing).
solutions.code:
cd /path/to/app
npm install
npm install express

problems.title: Error: listen EADDRINUSE: address already in use :::3000
problems.body:
Starting my Node dev server fails:
Error: listen EADDRINUSE: address already in use :::3000
Nothing else should be running.

solutions.body: Find and kill the process holding the port on Windows.
Find and kill the process holding the port on macOS or Linux.

problems.title: npm ERR! code ERESOLVE unable to resolve dependency tree
problems.body:
npm install fails:
npm ERR! code ERESOLVE
npm ERR! ERESOLVE unable to resolve dependency tree
npm ERR! Could not resolve dependency:
npm ERR! peer react@"^17.0.0" from some-ui-lib@2.3.0

solutions.body: Upgrade the library to a version whose peer range includes your React version, so the tree resolves cleanly.
solutions.code:
npm view some-ui-lib peerDependencies
npm install some-ui-lib@latest

solutions.body: Skip peer dependency resolution. Install succeeds but you may hit runtime errors if the library truly needs the older React.

problems.title: SyntaxError: Cannot use import statement outside a module
problems.body:
Running node index.js:
import express from 'express';
^^^^^^
SyntaxError: Cannot use import statement outside a module

solutions.body: Tell Node the package uses ES modules by adding "type": "module" to package.json, or rename the file to .mjs.

problems.title: Error: error:0308010C:digital envelope routines::unsupported
problems.body:
npm start on an older Create React App project fails on Node 18:
Error: error:0308010C:digital envelope routines::unsupported
  opensslErrorStack: [ 'error:03000086:digital envelope routines::initialization error' ],
  library: 'digital envelope routines',
  code: 'ERR_OSSL_EVP_UNSUPPORTED'

solutions.body: Upgrade to webpack 5 based tooling (react-scripts 5), which no longer uses the MD4 hash removed in OpenSSL 3.
Re-enable legacy OpenSSL algorithms. Works as a stopgap but keeps you on an unsupported build setup.

problems.title: npm ERR! code EACCES permission denied, mkdir '/usr/local/lib/node_modules'
problems.body:
npm install -g fails:
npm ERR! code EACCES
npm ERR! syscall mkdir
npm ERR! path /usr/local/lib/node_modules/typescript
npm ERR! Error: EACCES: permission denied, mkdir '/usr/local/lib/node_modules/typescript'

solutions.body: Don't use sudo. Install Node with a version manager (nvm) so global packages live in your home directory.
solutions.code:
curl -o- https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nvm-sh/nvm/v0.40.1/install.sh | bash
nvm install --lts
npm install -g typescript

problems.title: Blocked by CORS policy: No 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header
problems.body:
My React app at localhost:5173 calls my Express API at localhost:3000 and the browser shows:
Access to fetch at 'http://localhost:3000/api' from origin 'http://localhost:5173' has been blocked by CORS policy: No 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' header is present on the requested resource.

solutions.body: CORS must be allowed by the server. Add the cors middleware to Express and allow your frontend origin.

problems.title: TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'map')
problems.body:
My React component crashes on first render:
TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'map')
The data comes from a fetch in useEffect.

solutions.body: The first render happens before the fetch resolves. Initialise the state to an empty array (or guard with optional chaining).
